title: EAST Tokamak Demonstrates Novel DTP Plasma Regime — Physical Review Letters
detail: China's EAST (Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak) at the Institute of Plasma Physics (ASIPP) in Hefei demonstrated a new 'DTP' (Detached divertor and Turbulence-dominated Pedestal) plasma regime in a metal-wall tokamak environment — the first such demonstration in a metal-wall device. The regime simultaneously achieved partial divertor detachment, edge-localized-mode (ELM)-free high-confinement operation, and enhanced pedestal performance for approximately one minute. Published in Physical Review Letters (lead researcher: Prof. Xu Guosheng, ASIPP), the result is significant because it shows a potential path to managing extreme heat loads on the divertor — one of the most pressing engineering problems for commercial fusion reactors — without sacrificing plasma confinement quality. ELM-free high-confinement mode and divertor detachment are normally in tension; the DTP regime reconciles both simultaneously, offering a potential operational scenario for ITER and future power plants.

title: Zap Energy Appoints Zabrina Johal as CEO, Expands to Dual Fission-Fusion Strategy
detail: Seattle-based Zap Energy named Zabrina Johal as its new CEO and announced a significant strategic expansion: alongside its core sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch fusion research, the company will pursue an integrated nuclear strategy incorporating deployment of 50 MW small modular reactors (SMRs) based on the 4S (Super-Safe, Small, and Simple) fission design. Zap expects to begin generating revenue from the fission business within approximately one year, providing a commercial bridge while fusion technology matures. The pivot reflects wider pressures in private fusion financing — the rolling 12-month private investment rate has softened to ~$1.6B (April 2026) from its $2.64B mid-2025 peak — and mirrors moves by other fusion companies to diversify toward near-term revenues. Zap, a University of Washington spinoff, has raised $160M+. Its Z-pinch approach, which uses no magnets and relies on sheared-flow stabilization to confine plasma, remains the company's long-term commercial target.
